No.06

Does Bodhicitta Require Being Great and Saintly?

Starting from a single wish for good and a single act that helps another — finding the awakened heart in ordinary life.

Author's record · translated; the Chinese original is authoritative

Open in reading mode →

🔶Inquiry to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva

I asked Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva: what does it mean to arouse bodhicitta, the mind of awakening? For ordinary people and beginners, it sounds very far away — we feel we are not that great or that good.

🔶The Bodhisattva's Teaching

"Arousing the mind is not far; the moment a thought arises, it is near. Bodhi means awakening; mind means aspiration. It need not be a great vow or a grand resolve to be called bodhi; a single thought wishing good, a single act that benefits another — all of this is arousing the mind. The foolish see the Buddha's mind and feel small; the wise see that their own mind is the Buddha's mind. If you see another's suffering and feel pity, if you hear the Dharma and feel joy, if you can bear a small wrong without repaying it, if you wish to protect one life, one flower, one book — these are all sprouts of bodhicitta.

Do not be ashamed to speak of helping others across because you have not yet crossed yourself. Bodhicitta does not wait for perfection; it arises in ordinary thoughts and grows amid worldly toil. This is called 'true arousing of the mind'."

🔶Plain Rendering

The Bodhisattva said: Arousing bodhicitta is not something far out of reach; as soon as you have a kind thought, you are already close to it. "Bodhi" means awakening, and "mind" here means aspiration. So arousing bodhicitta is the heart that wishes to awaken, to do good, and to help all beings. It does not have to be a grand vow like those in the sutras; if you sincerely wish others well and are willing to do small things that benefit them, you are arousing bodhicitta.

Foolish people see the Buddha's mind and feel tiny, but the wise know that their own mind is, at its root, one with the Buddha's mind. When you see others suffering and feel compassion, when you hear the Dharma and feel joy, when you can face a little unkindness without striking back, when you are willing to protect a life, a flower, a book of scripture — these are the seeds of true bodhicitta. Do not think you cannot help others cross over just because you have not yet crossed; bodhicitta does not need to wait until your practice is complete.

It sprouts amid the dust of the world and grows within daily life. A heart aroused in this way is what is called "truly arousing bodhicitta".
